title: Arrow's theorem via Fourier analysis
abstract: This is a formalization in Lean 4 of Arrow's theorem for three-candidate elections as stated in Ryan O'Donnell's book "Analysis of Boolean Functions", Sec. 2.5, with a single voting rule applied to every pairwise election. The theorem states that every unanimous voting rule that always admits a Condorcet winner  must be a dictatorship, i.e. there must exist a voter that alone determines the outcome. Here voting rules are encoded by Boolean-valued functions on the Hamming cube. The proof follows the exposition given there, which is based on Gil Kalai's Fourier-analytic argument using the Walsh-Fourier transform. The version stated in the book  and formalized here is not the most general version of Arrow's theorem: for example, one may allow more than three candidates, or that the voting rules for each pairwise election are different. This formalization was entirely human-written.
